full_text_en:
**Shenzhen Basic Living Supplies Co., Ltd. v. Shenzhen Sipai Silicone Electronics Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of design patent**

**Ruling Summary**

Repeated infringement includes the following constituent elements: (1) the right infringed in the present action is the same right as that infringed in the previous action; (2) the infringer in the present action is the same subject as the infringer in the previous action; (3) the infringing product in the present action is the same product (in terms of infringement constitution) as the infringing product in the previous action; (4) the infringing act in the present action occurs after the judgment of the previous action takes effect and there is a reasonable time interval. An action brought by a right holder regarding repeated infringement does not constitute a repeated action, and the people's court shall accept it in accordance with the law.

**Plaintiff:** Shenzhen Basic Living Supplies Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Eastern Industrial Zone, Overseas Chinese Town, Nanshan District, Shenzhen.
**Legal Representative:** Chen Shi, General Manager of the company.

**Defendant:** Shenzhen Sipai Silicone Electronics Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Baohua Road, Longhua Street, Bao'an District, Shenzhen.
**Legal Representative:** Gan Xue, Chairman of the company.

The plaintiff, Shenzhen Basic Living Supplies Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Basic Living Company), filed a lawsuit with the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province against the defendant, Shenzhen Sipai Silicone Electronics Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Sipai Company), concerning a dispute over infringement of design patent.

**Plaintiff's Allegations:** The defendant, Sipai Company, by manufacturing, selling, and offering for sale the accused infringing product, infringed upon the design patent right involved in this case, and the infringement constituted repeated infringement, for which it should bear legal liability. The plaintiff requested the court to order: 1. Sipai Company to immediately cease manufacturing, selling, and offering for sale the infringing product, and immediately destroy the infringing products in stock and specialized production molds; 2. Sipai Company to compensate Basic Living Company for economic losses and reasonable expenses incurred in stopping the infringement, totaling RMB 1,000,000; 3. Sipai Company to bear all litigation costs in this case.

**Defendant's Defense:** Sipai Company argued that it did not manufacture, sell, or offer for sale the accused infringing product, and requested the court to dismiss all claims of the plaintiff, Basic Living Company.

**Facts Found by the Court at First Instance (Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court):**

On October 9, 2010, Chen Shi, the legal representative of the plaintiff Basic Living Company, filed an application with the State Intellectual Property Office for a design patent entitled "Card Case (A3308)," which was granted on April 6, 2011, under Patent No. ZL201030547929.9. On May 6, 2011, the patentee Chen Shi and Basic Living Company executed a "Patent Implementation License Authorization."

The patent in question consists of seven views from different angles. The design points are in the shape, and the view that best shows the design points is the front view. Viewed from the front, the overall shape is rectangular, composed of a box body and a cover. There is a rectangular hollow in the middle of the box body, and near the opening of the body (i.e., the top of the hollow) there is a round protrusion containing a magnet for fixing the cover when opened or closed. The cover is a rectangular object connected to the body, folding inward to form a closure. The part of the cover connected to the body is serrated. A round magnet is located near the top of the inner side of the cover. When folded, the cover magnet attracts the magnet of the body, forming a closed card case.

On May 28, 2014, under the supervision of a notary, the agent ad litem of the plaintiff Basic Living Company used a computer at the notary office to purchase the accused infringing product online. On June 4, 2014, the agent ad litem of Basic Living Company and the notary took delivery of a package containing the accused infringing product, thereby obtaining the accused infringing product (a white silicone card case). Upon comparison, the design of the accused infringing product was identical to the patented design.

Separately, on February 9, 2012, the plaintiff Basic Living Company had previously sued Sipai Company and Shenzhen Weiwenny Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Weiwenny Company) in the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court, alleging that the defendant Sipai Company manufactured and sold the accused infringing product, infringing upon the patent right in question. The plaintiff requested: "1. Order the two defendants to immediately cease manufacturing and selling the infringing product, and immediately destroy the specialized molds used for manufacturing the infringing product and the infringing products in stock; 2. Order the two defendants to compensate for economic losses of RMB 100,000, with the two defendants bearing joint liability; 3. Order the two defendants to bear the litigation costs and rights protection costs totaling RMB 2,000." The court rendered the Civil Judgment (2012) Shen Zhong Fa Zhi Min Chu Zi No. 250, finding: "Sipai Company and Weiwenny Company, without permission from Basic Living Company, manufactured and sold similar products that were similar in design to the patent in question, constituting joint infringement. Sipai Company and Weiwenny Company shall immediately cease the infringement and jointly compensate Basic Living Company for its economic losses." The judgment ordered: "1. Weiwenny Company and Sipai Company shall immediately cease infringing upon Basic Living Company's design patent right for the 'Card Case (S3308)' under Patent No. ZL201030547929.9, and destroy the infringing products in stock and specialized production molds; 2. Weiwenny Company and Sipai Company shall jointly compensate Basic Living Company for economic losses of RMB 30,000 within ten days from the effective date of this judgment; 3. Dismiss Basic Living Company's other claims." Weiwenny Company appealed the first-instance judgment. The Guangdong High People's Court, after trial, rendered the Civil Judgment (2012) Yue Gao Fa Min San Zhong Zi No. 406 on October 18, 2012, affirming the first-instance judgment. That judgment took effect on November 5, 2012. Upon comparison, the accused infringing product in this case is identical to the accused infringing product in that case.

**Opinion of the Court at First Instance (Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court):**

**I. Whether the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of the patent in question.** The accused infringing product "silicone card case" and the patented product "card case" are similar products. Upon comparison, the left and right views of the accused infringing product have obvious raised stripes, while the patent lacks this feature; the bottom of the accused infringing product has a long strip-shaped window, while the patent images show only a small opening at the bottom; apart from these, other designs are identical. The differences are not sufficiently distinctive. An ordinary consumer, through overall observation and comprehensive assessment, would find no substantial difference in overall visual effect. Therefore, the two should be considered similar, and the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of the patent in question.

**II. Whether the defendant Sipai Company manufactured, sold, or offered for sale the accused infringing product.** Sipai Company publicly displayed and promoted images of the accused infringing product on its Alibaba online store and official website. This conduct constitutes an offer for sale of the accused infringing product. Therefore, the plaintiff Basic Living Company's allegation that Sipai Company offered the infringing product for sale is established, and the court supports it. However, Basic Living Company's allegation that Sipai Company manufactured and sold the accused infringing product cannot be substantiated. This allegation is essentially a repeated action regarding the case (2012) Yue Gao Fa Min San Zhong Zi No. 406. First, the plaintiff in both cases is the same person, Basic Living Company; the defendant includes Sipai Company in both cases. Although the defendant in Case No. 406 also included Weiwenny Company, Basic Living Company's claims in this regard were all directed against Sipai Company, and the entity that should bear responsibility is still Sipai Company. Second, the two cases involve the same legal relationship and the same legal facts. Both cases are infringement damage disputes filed by Basic Living Company based on the belief that Sipai Company manufactured and sold products infringing upon its patent right. Although the time of the alleged acts differs between the two cases, the basic content and facts involved are the same. Given that the effective judgment has already made determinations and addressed the matter, the court applies the principle of *ne bis in idem* (res judicata) and will not hear this part of Basic Living Company's claims.

**III. Regarding the assumption of legal liability.** The defendant Sipai Company, without the patentee's consent, offered for sale the accused infringing product for the purpose of production and operation, constituting infringement upon the patent in question, and shall bear tort liability. The plaintiff Basic Living Company requested the court to order Sipai Company to compensate for its economic losses and reasonable expenses for rights protection. However, Basic Living Company provided no evidence proving the actual losses caused by Sipai Company's offer for sale or the profits gained by Sipai Company. It only provided relevant bills totaling RMB 5,587.86 to substantiate the reasonable expenses for rights protection. Therefore, the court supports this part of the reasonable expenses. The court does not support Basic Living Company's claim for compensation, and Basic Living Company shall bear the litigation costs incurred for this part.

In conclusion, the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 11(2), Article 59(2), Article 65 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 8, 10, 11 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases, Article 124(5) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Procedure, rendered the following judgment on December 15, 2014:

1. Shenzhen Sipai Silicone Electronics Co., Ltd. shall immediately cease offering for sale products infringing upon Shenzhen Basic Living Supplies Co., Ltd.'s patent right under ZL201030547929.9;
2. Shenzhen Sipai Silicone Electronics Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate Shenzhen Basic Living Supplies Co., Ltd. for reasonable expenses for rights protection totaling RMB 5,587.86;
3. Dismiss Shenzhen Basic Living Supplies Co., Ltd.'s other claims.

Basic Living Company appealed the first-instance judgment to the Guangdong High People's Court, arguing: (1) The appellee Sipai Company's acts of manufacturing and selling the accused infringing product in this case constitute new infringement acts. Repeated infringement should be punished more severely. (2) The first-instance court's determination that Sipai Company's manufacturing and selling of the accused infringing product did not constitute repeated infringement but a repeated lawsuit, and thus holding Sipai Company not liable for compensation, is unfair. (3) The first-instance court found that Sipai Company offered the accused infringing product for sale but did not order it to bear compensation liability, only ordering payment of reasonable rights protection costs, which is an indulgence of infringement. In conclusion, Basic Living Company requested the second-instance court to ascertain the facts and amend the judgment: 1. Revoke the first-instance civil judgment; 2. Order Sipai Company to immediately cease manufacturing and selling the infringing product, and immediately destroy the specialized equipment, molds, and infringing products in stock used for manufacturing the infringing product; 3. Order Sipai Company to compensate for economic losses and reasonable expenses incurred in stopping the infringement totaling RMB 1,000,000; 4. Order Sipai Company to bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances.

The appellee Sipai Company argued: (1) The accused infringing product sold by Sipai Company in this case is the same product as the accused infringing product in the previous action, thus it is not a new infringement act. The appellant Basic Living Company's lawsuit constitutes a repeated lawsuit. Sipai Company sold only this one accused infringing product, and the first-instance judgment correctly held Sipai Company not liable for compensation. (2) Although Sipai Company offered the accused infringing product for sale, this was due to a product that was inadvertently left on the online store when infringing products were removed. The first-instance court's order that Sipai Company only pay reasonable rights protection costs is correct. (3) Basic Living Company filed several infringement lawsuits against Sipai Company simultaneously. In other cases, the first-instance court ordered compensation exceeding RMB 110,000. Therefore, it is reasonable that this case did not impose compensation liability. In conclusion, Sipai Company argued that the first-instance judgment found clear facts and correctly applied the law, and requested the second-instance court to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

Upon second-instance trial, the Guangdong High People's Court confirmed the facts found at first instance.

**Opinion of the Court at Second Instance (Guangdong High People's Court):**

The issues in dispute in this case are: whether the appellee Sipai Company engaged in manufacturing and selling the accused infringing product; whether Sipai Company's selling conduct should be treated as a repeated lawsuit or repeated infringement; and the legal liability Sipai Company should bear.

**I. Whether the appellee Sipai Company manufactured or sold the accused infringing product.** According to the notarial deeds provided by the appellant Basic Living Company: On May 28, 2014, under the supervision of a notary, the agent ad litem of Basic Living Company used a computer at the notary office to purchase the accused infringing product online. On June 4, 2014, the agent ad litem of Basic Living Company and the notary took delivery of a package containing the accused infringing product, thereby obtaining the accused infringing product (a white silicone card case). The two notarial deeds recorded the complete process of Basic Living Company's online purchase and receipt of the accused infringing product. Sipai Company also acknowledged this fact. Therefore, it can be determined that Sipai Company engaged in selling the accused infringing product. Additionally, Basic Living Company alleged that Sipai Company manufactured the accused infringing product, which Sipai Company denied. Since the white silicone card case did not indicate a manufacturer or product mark, and Basic Living Company did not submit other evidence proving that Sipai Company manufactured the accused infringing product, the second-instance court does not support Basic Living Company's claim that Sipai Company cease manufacturing the accused infringing product. In conclusion, the second-instance court finds that Sipai Company engaged in selling and offering for sale the accused infringing product.

**II. Whether the appellee Sipai Company's selling conduct should be treated as a repeated lawsuit or repeated infringement.** Article 247 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where a party files another lawsuit regarding a matter already brought to court during the litigation process or after the judgment takes effect, and the following conditions are met simultaneously, it constitutes a repeated lawsuit: (1) the parties in the subsequent action are the same as those in the prior action; (2) the subject matter of the subsequent action is the same as that of the prior action; (3) the claims in the subsequent action are the same as those in the prior action, or the claims in the subsequent action essentially negate the result of the prior judgment. If a party files a repeated lawsuit, the court shall rule not to accept it; if already accepted, the court shall rule to dismiss the action, unless otherwise provided by law or judicial interpretation. From the facts of this case: First, after the Civil Judgment (2012) Yue Gao Fa Min San Zhong Zi No. 406 took effect, the appellant Basic Living Company again sued Sipai Company to the court. The plaintiff in the prior case and the plaintiff in the subsequent case are both Basic Living Company. One of the defendants in the prior case, Sipai Company, is the same as the defendant in the subsequent case. Therefore, the parties in the prior and subsequent cases are substantially the same. Second, the subject matter of the prior action was to determine whether Sipai Company manufactured and sold the accused infringing product in February 2012. The subject matter of the subsequent action is to determine whether, after the prior judgment took effect, Sipai Company manufactured, sold, or offered for sale the accused infringing product in May and June 2014. The time periods of the infringing acts pointed to by the subject matter of the prior and subsequent actions are different. Finally, the claims in the prior action were: order Sipai Company to immediately cease the manufacturing and selling infringing acts discovered in February 2012, destroy the specialized molds and infringing products in stock; compensate for economic losses of RMB 100,000, and bear litigation costs and rights protection costs. The claims in the subsequent action are: order Sipai Company to immediately cease the manufacturing, selling, and offering for sale infringing acts rediscovered in May and June 2014 after the prior judgment took effect, destroy the infringing products in stock and specialized production molds; compensate Basic Living Company for economic losses and reasonable expenses incurred in stopping the infringement totaling RMB 1,000,000, and bear all litigation costs in this case. Thus, the claims in the subsequent action are not the same as those in the prior action, nor do they essentially negate the result of the prior judgment. In conclusion, the second-instance court finds that the subsequent action does not meet the statutory requirements for a repeated lawsuit.

From the effective date of the court's judgment ordering cessation of infringement, the infringer shall not engage in further acts of infringement. However, since repeated infringement involves obvious subjective fault and constitutes a more serious infringement, the people's court is always very cautious in determining whether repeated infringement exists. According to the facts found in this case: First, the time of the manufacturing and selling acts of the accused infringing product in the prior action was February 2012, and the final judgment took effect on November 5, 2012. The time of the offer for sale and sale on the website in the subsequent action was in May and June 2014. There was a period of one and a half years from the effective date of the prior judgment to the rediscovery of the infringing acts in the subsequent action. This excludes the scenario where it was objectively difficult for the appellee Sipai Company to recall and destroy the accused infringing product within a short time after the prior judgment took effect. Second, the subsequent action concerns Sipai Company's offer for sale on its own website and direct sale of the accused infringing product. This excludes the possibility that the accused infringing product was a remnant product from the prior action accidentally discovered in the market, or that it was deliberately planted on Sipai Company. Third, Sipai Company's claim that the offer for sale on its website was due to negligence in not removing the product for two years, and that the product purchased in the notarial purchase was the only product it had sold in two years, is inconsistent with common sense. The second-instance court does not accept this argument. Fourth, the design of the accused infringing product in the subsequent action is identical to that in the prior action. Given that the prior effective judgment had already confirmed the infringement, it is clear that the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of the patent in question, with no difficulty in determining infringement. Finally, if the reasoning of the first-instance judgment were followed—that as long as the prior action had already ruled on the defendant's manufacturing and selling of infringing products, the plaintiff could not sue the defendant again for similar infringement acts—this would mean that after the prior judgment takes effect, even if the defendant commits similar infringement acts, there would be no risk of being sued again. This clearly contradicts the legislative intent that repeated infringement should be punished more severely and would encourage malicious infringing acts. In conclusion, the second-instance court finds that Sipai Company's conduct constitutes repeated infringement. The first-instance judgment's determination that the appellant Basic Living Company's action constituted a repeated lawsuit is improper, and the second-instance court corrects this.

3. Legal Liability of Appellee Sipai Company. Without the patentee's consent, Sipai Company offered for sale and sold the accused infringing product for production and business purposes, constituting infringement of the patent-in-suit, and shall bear civil liability for cessation of infringement and compensation for losses. In this case, as it is difficult to determine the losses of the right holder, the profits gained by the infringer, or the patent licensing fee, the court of second instance comprehensively considered the following factors to determine the amount of damages at its discretion: First, on October 9, 2010, the patentee filed an application with the National Intellectual Property Administration for a design patent entitled "Cardholder (S3308)," which was granted on April 6, 2011. The patent protection period is now more than half over, yet the patent remains valid, demonstrating that the patent-in-suit has certain market value. Second, the infringing acts included both sales and offers for sale through the company's website, indicating a relatively serious nature of infringement and a greater negative market impact on the patentee. Third, the infringer is a repeat infringer with obvious subjective fault and serious infringement circumstances. Fourth, the amount of compensation in the previous judgment was RMB 30,000. For repeat infringement, the amount of compensation should be determined at a level higher than that in the previous judgment to impose a deterrent. Finally, the court of first instance verified that Appellant Basic Living Company incurred reasonable expenses for enforcing its rights in this case, including fees for electronic evidence preservation, purchase of infringing products, notarization, and attorney fees, totaling RMB 5,587.86. The court of second instance affirms this amount. In summary, within the scope of statutory damages, the court of second instance determines at its discretion that Sipai Company shall compensate Basic Living Company for economic losses (including reasonable expenses for enforcement of rights) in the amount of RMB 100,000. As for the other claims of Basic Living Company, due to insufficient evidence, the court of second instance dismisses them in accordance with the law.

In summary, some of Appellant Basic Living Company's grounds for appeal are established and are supported by the court of second instance. The first-instance judgment contained unclear findings of fact and errors in the application of law, which are corrected by the court of second instance in accordance with the law. Pursuant to Article 11, Paragraph 2; Article 59, Paragraph 2; and Article 65, Paragraph 2 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China; Articles 8, 10, and 11 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases; Article 247 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China; and Article 170, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court on November 3, 2016, rendered the following judgment:

1. Revise Item 3 of the Civil Judgment (2014) Shen Zhong Fa Zhi Min Chu Zi No. 552 of the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, which dismissed the other claims of Shenzhen Basic Living Products Co., Ltd.

2. Amend Item 1 of the Civil Judgment (2014) Shen Zhong Fa Zhi Min Chu Zi No. 552 of the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province to read: Shenzhen Sipai Silicone Electronics Co., Ltd. shall immediately cease offering for sale and selling products that infringe the patent right No. ZL201030547929.9 owned by Shenzhen Basic Living Products Co., Ltd.;

3. Amend Item 2 of the Civil Judgment (2014) Shen Zhong Fa Zhi Min Chu Zi No. 552 of the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province to read: Shenzhen Sipai Silicone Electronics Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate Shenzhen Basic Living Products Co., Ltd. for economic losses and reasonable expenses for enforcing its rights amounting to RMB 100,000;

4. Dismiss the other claims of Shenzhen Basic Living Products Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
